hood_landmark.Temple Bar: cobbled lanes centred on the famous red Temple Bar pub
hood_landmark.Ballsbridge: Aviva Stadium amid embassy-lined Victorian avenues
hood_landmark.Rathmines: the copper-domed Church of Mary Immaculate on the main street
hood_landmark.The Liberties: the Guinness Storehouse at St James's Gate
hood_landmark.Smithfield: Jameson Distillery Bow St. on the old cobbled market square

avoid.reason: Pickpocketing and anti-social behaviour around O'Connell St, the north inner city and some Luas stops at night

hood_desc: Temple Bar is Dublin's cobbled tourist and nightlife hub of pubs, live music and revelry, lively but pricey, best for partygoers and first-timers wanting to be in the thick of it.
Ballsbridge is a leafy, affluent embassy district of Georgian and Victorian homes, upscale hotels and rugby at the Aviva Stadium, suited to luxury and quieter, refined stays.
Rathmines is a popular residential and student neighborhood just south of the center, with relaxed cafes, pubs and good value, appealing to budget travelers and longer stays.
The Liberties is one of Dublin's oldest working-class quarters, home to the Guinness Storehouse and whiskey distilleries, gritty and increasingly hip for history and craft-drink fans.
Smithfield is a regenerated northside square district around the Jameson distillery with cocktail bars and a cinema, a trendy, up-and-coming base for younger travelers.

water.note: Tap water is safe and well-regulated across the city.

transit.pay: Get a TFI Leap Card — fares are far cheaper than cash singles, and the 90-minute fare (about 2 EUR) covers transfers between bus, Luas and DART. The Leap Visitor Card (1 day ~10 EUR, 3 days ~20 EUR/~US$23, 7 days ~40 EUR) gives unlimited travel and is sold at Dublin Airport and city Leap agents. Contactless bank cards are not yet accepted on city buses, Luas or DART.
transit.hours: Buses run roughly 5am-11:30pm with several 24-hour routes and Nitelink on weekend nights; Luas runs about 5:30am-12:30am.
